sentences.text: Majungasaurus was a medium-sized theropod reaching about 7 meters in length and weighing over a ton.
This dinosaur featured very short forelimbs and longer, stocky hindlimbs, alongside a wider skull with rough bone on the snout and a single rounded horn.
First found in 1896 and initially misidentified as Megalosaurus, the genus was formally established by René Lavocat in 1955 after he described a theropod lower jaw.
Later fieldwork in 1996, part of a project starting in 1993, uncovered a spectacularly complete skull preserved in exquisite detail.
As the apex predator, it likely used a bite-and-hold strategy similar to modern cats, supported by its broader snout compared to other relatives.
Its skull decorations may have aided in competition, while giant snakes might have preyed on young individuals.
Originally described as Megalosaurus, a related skull fragment was once thought to be a synonym but is now placed in the subfamily Majungasaurinae.
Living between 70 and 66 million years ago, all specimens come from the Maevarano Formation in northwestern Madagascar, a coastal floodplain with sandy river channels.
Scientists debated whether the skull fragment belonged to Majungasaurus or another group, and whether abelisaurids formed separate eastern and western clades.
